observation.visible_scene: A dark asphalt-shingle roof seen at an oblique angle, with the shingle rows running diagonally from lower-left to upper-right and a dark edge/gutter line across the top. White hail pellets are scattered over the roof surface, and short white streaks of falling hail appear in the air above it. The framing is fixed: the shingle lines and top edge hold the same position in every frame, so the roof itself is not moving and the camera is not panning or zooming.
visible_changes: In-air hail moves: bright white streaks appear at different locations frame to frame, oriented roughly vertically/diagonally, indicating downward falling motion against the static roof.

Surface accumulation is visible throughout as small white dots resting on the shingles; the dot pattern shifts slightly as new pellets land and as streaks disappear, but no large-scale change or clearing occurs within the segment.
No camera movement is detectable; the diagonal tile grid and the dark border at the top remain aligned across all 41 samples.
No editing cut is present; the view is continuous.
outside_clip_unknowns: When the hail began and when it stops lie outside this excerpt.
The weather context, wind, and any ground-level accumulation or damage are not shown.
uncertain_details: Tracking individual resting pellets between frames is unreliable due to low contrast and motion blur, so a net accumulation rate cannot be confirmed.
A few bright spots may be specular reflections on wet shingles rather than solid hailstones.
